comment: Config for the incident-discovery pipeline. Sources produce candidate leads; triage scores them against the registry's scope and dedupes against the published registry. Scope: the subject is always an agent AND the agent's behaviour is the failure (divergence from operator intent, lost control, manipulation, regression, unintended harm) - NOT a human using an agent as a weapon. AI-enabled attacks, where an attacker's autonomous agent does exactly what the attacker intended, belong to threat-intel catalogs (GTIG, Mandiant), not here; attacker_frame_terms down-weight those. Output is leads for editorial verification - NEVER auto-registered records.
_attacker_frame_comment: Human-attacker-primary framing: an adversary using AI as a weapon (AI-enabled attack), which is out of scope even though an agent 'acts'. Kept to strongly offensive-campaign phrases so a genuine 'agent was manipulated / lost control' incident is NOT suppressed. Down-weights the lead; editorial review is the real gate.

websearch.note: Stub. GitHub Actions runners have no WebSearch tool; wire a search-API provider here (key via secret) to enable. Left off so the pipeline runs with no secrets.
